text:
ari-sales: FYI - Globex procurement is asking us to remove the Export Control clause from the MSA because their vendor policy forbids vendor-side export language. PO and SOW are signed, but legal/procurement are blocking on this. Need quick risk call + signature routing guidance.

nina-legal: Can you paste the exact clause they want removed? Is this a sanctions thing or more about data residency/subprocessor visibility? cc @kevin-security

ari-sales: Here's the snippet they flagged:

```
Export Control: Customer shall not export, re-export, transfer, or disclose any Redwood technology or data outside the United States or to any person or entity on restricted party lists. Customer will comply with U.S. export control and sanctions laws.
```

nina-legal: If they insist on deleting, we need substitute language. Proposal: "Parties will comply with applicable export and sanctions laws. Customer may request reasonable evidence of subprocessors' compliance; Redwood will not knowingly permit restricted-party use." Would that get them over the line?

marta-ops: Heads up - they're also requesting HSM key control in the DPA and an SLA with 10ms p95 for embeddings. That's not achievable on Hosted Dedicated in eu-west-1 for the traffic shape they described. We should counter with a 50ms p95 + credits schedule, or offer Private deployment with HSM.

kevin-security: HSM/KMS control is feasible for Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys, not for shared hosted. On export: Ukraine as a subprocessor country isn't a blanket block but we still need subprocessors list and basic screening. Do we have their subprocessors list?

ari-sales: They listed a subcontractor in Ukraine that handles preprocessing. Procurement keeps saying "foreign vendor" and wants the export clause removed entirely. They also want signature routing: CFO + legal countersign only (no technical sign-off).

elena-eng: :thinking_face: Also 10ms p95 for embeddings at ~3k concurrent reqs and 512 token averages is unrealistic. We can offer model-level guidance: limit request size <=512 tokens for the SLA, enable batching hints, and suggest quantized model variants to reduce latency.

nina-legal: OK. I'll draft redlines for the MSA and DPA: (1) Replace specific US-only export language with a neutral compliance clause, (2) Add a subprocessors disclosure paragraph, (3) Add an HSM opt-in addendum stub for Private deployments, (4) Add SLA addendum limiting p95 commitments to requests <=512 tokens and specifying credit schedule.

ari-sales: Can you also include an order form addendum for Net30 PO routing + EDI invoice field? Procurement specifically said they need PO + EDI mapping for AP. I need to send to them by EOD.

marta-ops: Net30 looks fine pending credit check. For the SLA/latency redline we'll attach a performance appendix with region-specific p95s and a fallback model variant. I'll draft numbers for eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

finance-bot: Credit check passed. Approve net30 up to $200k monthly spend for Globex (automated).

nina-legal: Will prepare redline bundle (MSA+DPA+SLA addendum+order form addendum) and set signature route to be countersigned by CFO (customer) and Redwood Legal. We can accept DocuSign for this customer; confirm if procurement requires any special signer mapping.

ari-sales: Procurement needs invoice to ap@globex.com, PO on invoice header, and EDI field X12/850 mapping with vendor id 9987. Also they want an internal attestation that subprocessors have SOC2 or ISO27001.

kevin-security: We can produce subprocessors list and SOC2/ISO statements for qualified subprocessors. For any subprocessor where we can't provide certification we'll add a mitigations paragraph.

ari-sales: Sweet. I'll bundle and send. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
